findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients are not upgraded with the Clients schema
findings.body: `init` returns immediately when the realm already has an admin-permissions client. A realm that enabled FGAP V2 before this change therefore keeps only the old Users resource/scopes: it never receives the Clients all-resource or the new `configure`, `map-roles-client-scope`, and `map-roles-composite` scopes. Creating a per-client permission then attempts to attach every Clients scope and fails with `No scopes found`, while global-client permission evaluation can also encounter a missing resource. Add a non-destructive schema backfill/migration path for existing admin-permissions clients.

findings.title: The all-clients manage permission does not grant list/view access
findings.body: `canView()` recognizes only the all-clients `view` scope, unlike `canView(ClientModel)`, which reaches `canManage(client)` through `canConfigure(client)`. The inherited `canList()` and client-scope listing checks depend on this zero-argument method, so an administrator granted only the all-clients `manage` scope can create, update, and delete clients but cannot list them. This contradicts the intended manage permission behavior and makes the added `testManageAllClients` listing expectation fail. Include `manage` here (or delegate through `canManage()`).

findings.title: Role-mapping checks drop the built-in manage-clients authorization
findings.body: `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` only evaluate V2 authorization resources. They do not preserve the `MANAGE_CLIENTS` admin-role fallback used by the other client checks, so a normal realm-management administrator with `manage-clients` is denied client-role assignment and composite-role changes whenever FGAP V2 is enabled unless separate V2 policies are created. The map-role checks need to honor the built-in management role (and the intended manage-scope inheritance, if applicable) before evaluating the resource scope.

findings.title: Deleting a client leaves its V2 authorization resource and policies behind
findings.body: The client-removal listener now runs only when the legacy `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` feature is enabled. In a V2-only deployment, a `ClientRemovedEvent` is ignored, while the per-client resource and its scope permissions live under the admin-permissions resource server and have no foreign-key relationship to the deleted target client. They remain orphaned indefinitely; if a client with the same internal ID is later restored/imported, `getOrCreateResource` resolves the old resource by name and the deleted client's grants become effective for the new client. Add V2-specific resource/policy cleanup on client removal.
